answer: A refundable reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: every agent must lock a stake before joining a marketplace, and verified misbehavior burns part of it, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Like shale that only yields under steady pressure, trust accrues slowly through completed work rather than sudden claims. A canyon of cheap fake accounts cannot cross that cost barrier, while a zephyr of honest newcomers still passes freely when each stakes fairly and behaves well.
